#en: This forgotten cryo lab hangs between star systems like a discarded hypothesis, its power failing in fits and starts, emergency lights stuttering over frost-fogged corridors and half-dead monitors. It matters because Torque chose it, not for cover, but for control: a place where he can scrub signatures, reroute life support, and bury what he has become in rusted hardware no corporation will ever bother to audit. Here he has been unspooling Iyla Korr's trail and everyone else's, cross-checking crash logs from freighters and luxury liners alike, deciding which truths to exhume and which to freeze forever, and now he is close to erasing the last proof that any of this was engineered. If he finishes, the pattern of bad drives, missing recall orders, and dead witnesses will become just another rumor, like the oldest version of this story, already smudged by bar talk about a dataslate in the dust, a lonely hut full of glitching telemetry, a silent ship on the edge of nowhere, and a UC warship whose black-box reports were never meant to see daylight.
zh: 这座被遗忘的冷冻实验室像一份被丢弃的假设悬在星系之间，电力断断续续地衰竭，应急灯在多霜迷雾的走廊与半死的显示器上闪烁。它要紧，是因为"扭矩"选中了它——不是为了掩护，而是为了控制：一个他能擦净签名、重接生命维持，并把自己变成的样子埋进公司永远不会费心审计的锈蚀硬件里的地方。在这里，他一直在展开艾拉·科尔的痕迹与所有其他人的痕迹，交叉核对货船与豪华邮轮的坠毁日志，决定哪些真相该被挖出、哪些该被永久冻结；如今他离抹掉"这一切都是人为设计"的最后证据只差一步。若他完工，坏引擎、失踪召回令与死掉证人的模式就会变成又一则传闻——就像这个故事最古老的版本一样，早已被酒吧闲谈抹淡：尘土里一块数据板、一座满是故障遥测的孤独小屋、一艘天涯边缘的沉默船只，以及一艘"黑匣报告本不该见天日"的联殖军舰。

#en: No one logs a relay out here by mistake; an asteroid field this thin, this far from any declared corridor, exists to lose signals, not anchor them, which is exactly why someone like Luna would lace her work through its static. The rocks and dust give cover to whatever she tested first, the bad corridors and half-finished vanish routes that never made it onto official charts, and to anyone now hired to erase those traces before a hunter can read them. Out in this drift, there is no jurisdiction, no flight control, only the raw noise of grav drives and broken stone, and somewhere inside that noise is the pattern she has been refining since her first ship went missing. Stories about a ghost in the traffic have passed from LIST clerks to GalBank pilots and bar-front fixers, picking up new details every retelling, but the only solid things so far were a protection escort whose route logs did not match its manifest and whispers that certain beacons in dead space repeat the same warped checksum, like an echo waiting for someone stubborn enough to chase it.
zh: 没人在这种地方误建中继；一片这么稀薄、离任何申报走廊这么远的小行星带，生来就是为了让信号失灵、而非锚定它们——这正是像露娜那样的人会把作品编织进它静电里的原因。岩石与尘土为"她最先测试的东西"提供掩护：那些从未进入官方星图的坏走廊与半途而废的消失航线，以及任何如今受雇、要在猎人读懂它们之前擦掉那些痕迹的人。在这片漂流带里，没有管辖，没有飞行控制，只有引力引擎与碎石的原始噪声；而那片噪声里的某处，是她自第一艘船失踪以来一直在精炼的模式。关于交通中一个幽灵的故事，已从独立盟文书传到盖尔银行飞行员与酒吧门前的掮客，每次重述都添了新细节；可目前为止唯一确凿的东西，是一艘航线日志与舱单不符的护航船，以及"死寂太空中某些信标重复着同一段扭曲校验和"的低语——像一道等着某个足够固执的人去追的回声。

#en: The empty barracks still hum with recycled air and old orders, a forgotten outpost built to outlast the Colony War and then quietly abandoned when the treaties came. Rivet chose this place because no one counts the dead here anymore, and because the walls are already wired for controlled demolitions and silent drills; it is the perfect frame to cut apart and vanish inside. His grav logs, stolen drives, and the star map that ties every gutted wreck together will be staged to jump from here, slipping past Freestar patrol routes and UC scrutiny alike. If he succeeds, the pattern he has been tracing in secret will move beyond anyone's reach, along with the last unedited record of what really happened in those forgotten battles. From the frozen carcass in deep space where a stranded cutter dropped Rivet's name, to the quiet farm where Waggoner soil hid Deimos-marked scrap, to the garrison stripped along precise load-bearing seams, every step has pointed to one hand testing structures, erasing witnesses, and following that same impossible signal through the wreckage.
zh: 那座空营房仍带着循环空气与旧命令的嗡鸣，一座为熬过殖民地大战而建、随后在条约到来时被悄悄弃置的被遗忘前哨。"铆钉"选中这里，是因为这里再没人清点死者，也因为墙壁本就为受控爆破与静默演练布好了线；它是拆解与消失的完美框架。他的引力日志、偷来的引擎，以及那张把每一具被掏空残骸连起来的星图，都将从这里跃迁出去，滑过自由星系联盟巡逻航线与联殖审查。若他成功，他一直在暗中追查的模式就会移出任何人的触及范围，连同那些被遗忘的战斗中真正发生了什么的最后未删改记录。从深空中一名搁浅切割船船员念出"铆钉"名字的冷冻残骸，到瓦戈纳的土壤藏着火卫二标记废料的安静农场，再到沿精确承重接缝被剥光的驻军，每一步都指向同一只手：测试结构、抹掉证人，并循着同一道不可能的信号穿过残骸。

#en: Places like The Clinic are supposed to scrub the blood off history, pin it behind glass with a comforting plaque, and call that healing. That is why the trail bends here: if anyone tried to turn a battlefield horror into a neat case study, it would be the station that survived a war by changing hands instead of course. Somewhere in its curated corridors there will be a sanitized version of what happened at that garrison, and tucked behind that, the parts the UC was glad to misplace and Freestar has no incentive to dig up. Staff whisper different stories when they think no one is listening; some fear what an unedited record might stir up, others like the safety that comes from not asking questions.  \nUp to now, the path has been fragments and contradictions: a stray slate on a forgotten rock, a derelict patrol ship still following half-erased orders, conflicting mentions of the same medic in logs that should never overlap. Everything points back to one incident no one wants to own, and a man who walked out of it still answering to commands nobody remembers signing.
zh: 像"星际诊所号"这样的地方，本应把血从历史里擦净，用一块让人安心的铭牌把它钉在玻璃后面，然后称之为疗愈。这就是线索拐向这里的原因：若有人曾试图把一场战地恐怖变成一个整齐的案例研究，那一定会是那座靠"易主而非改航"在战争中幸存下来的星际站。在它策展过的走廊里某处，会有关于那座驻军所发生之事的净化版本；而在那之后，则藏着联殖乐于弄丢、自由星系联盟没有动力去挖出的部分。员工们在以为没人听时会讲不同的故事；有些人害怕一份未删改记录会搅起什么，另一些人则喜欢"不问问题"带来的安全。  \n到目前为止，这条路是碎片与矛盾：被遗忘岩石上一块散落数据板、一具仍服从半擦除命令的弃置巡逻舰，以及在那些本绝不该重叠的日志里对同一名医疗兵的矛盾提及。一切都被指回一起没人愿意认领的事件，以及一个从中走出、仍在回应没人记得签署过的命令的人。

#en: The Deserted Relay Station hangs at the edge of the system like a dead nerve in the grav lattice, perfectly placed where old UC traffic once converged and where Vector can now listen to every tremor in the lanes. Its dishes have been twisted into a spider's web of jury-rigged antennas, feeding his stolen diagnostics and anomaly models into a humming core that treats the whole sector as a laboratory. Here, at the intersection of abandoned infrastructure and unstable readings, he can attempt the final proof he has been chasing since the testbed freighter died, a localized grav twitch big enough to force the truth into the open or tear this orbit apart. A misrouted UC maintenance order, an unsigned transfer request in New Atlantis, and a delayed pirate intercept have all nudged this confrontation here, now. Earlier, the quiet failures at the research site, the corrupted logs in high orbit, and the redacted disputes buried in Calyx files all traced the same pattern of staged "accidents" and missing data, pointing to the same exhausted analyst running out of places to hide.
zh: 那座"被遗弃的中继站"像引力网格里一根死掉的神经悬在星系边缘，恰好位于旧联殖交通曾汇聚之处，也是"向量"如今能听见航道每一次颤抖之处。它的天线盘被扭成一张由临时拼凑天线构成的蛛网，把他的偷来诊断与异常模型喂进一个把整个星区当作实验室的嗡鸣核心。在这里、在废弃基础设施与不稳定读数的交汇处，他能尝试自那艘试验台货船死亡以来他一直追逐的最终证明：一次足以迫使真相暴露、或把这条轨道撕开局部的引力抽搐。一份被错投的联殖维护令、新亚特兰蒂斯城里一份未签名的转运请求，以及一次被延误的海盗拦截，都把这面对撞推到了此地、此刻。早先，研究场址的安静故障、高轨道里损坏的日志，以及埋在花萼文件里的涂黑争执，全都追溯出同样的"人造事故与失踪数据"模式，指向同一名"快没地方可藏"的疲惫分析员。

#en: The farm is the first wound on the map, a place the banks wrote off and the locals forgot, which makes it perfect for hiding the kind of record no one wants audited. Its fields lie fallow under a thin sky, but the power feed to the main house still hums, and there are fresh boot tracks in the dust that do not belong to settlers. Uniform Blackguard watch the place with the stiff patience of contractors told to guard something they are not allowed to open, their black-and-white marks stark against sun-bleached siding; whatever is on that farm terminal, it scared someone enough to pay for silence. In town, stories about the foreclosure and the family who vanished never quite match, and every time the argument starts over who was at fault, it ends in a shrug and a change of subject, like everybody agreed not to dig any deeper. So far the trail is thin but steady: a dead spacer clutching stolen audit clips, a homestead that settled its debts after it was already empty, and scattered whispers that the same unseen hand keeps touching accounts from Akila to forgotten LIST rocks.
zh: 那座农场是地图上的第一道伤口，一个银行核销、当地人遗忘的地方，这让它成了藏起一份"没人想被审计之记录"的完美地点。它的田地在稀薄天空下休耕，可主屋的电力馈线仍在嗡鸣，尘土里有不属于定居者的新鲜靴印。"黑卫制服"以那种"被告知看守某样不许打开之物"的承包商的僵硬耐心看着这地方，他们黑白分明的标记在被晒白的墙板上格外醒目；无论那座农场终端上有什么，它都吓到了某人，吓到有人出钱买沉默。在镇上，关于那笔止赎与那户消失人家的说法从来对不上，而每次争起"谁该负责"，都以耸肩与换话题告终，仿佛所有人都同意不再深挖。目前为止，这条线索稀薄却稳定：一名死掉太空劫匪紧抓着偷来的审计片段、一座在早已空掉之后才清偿债务的农庄，以及零散低语说同一只无形之手不断从阿基拉城伸向被遗忘的独立盟岩石、触碰账户。

#en: No court, no committee, would ever authorize a strike here, which is why he chose it; this forgotten Deimos scrapyard is where the company buried its mistakes under rust, slag, and sealed manifests, then agreed to never speak of them again. The ground is a lattice of failed grav mounts and warped frames, each plate stamped with dates and serials no one in New Atlantis admits exist, and Rivet has threaded himself through that history like a live wire. He has been stripping these carcasses for parts, building one last test frame and rigging the yard with "lessons" to collapse around anyone who gets close, all while consolidating the telemetry and design logs that prove who really cut corners. If he completes his work here, the evidence disappears in a plume of twisted metal and decompressed air, and the pattern of quiet disasters he followed from a Ranger's field notes to this very graveyard becomes just another rumor spacers pretend not to remember: anonymous schematics on a dataslate in the dust, erased audits on Deimos, and a trail of ships saved or shattered by the same invisible hand.
zh: 没有法庭、没有委员会会批准在这里发动打击，这正是他选中它的原因；这座被遗忘的火卫二废料场，是公司把错误埋进锈、渣与密封舱单之下、然后同意永不再提的地方。地面是一张由失效引力支架与扭曲框架构成的网格，每块板材都盖着新亚特兰蒂斯城里没人承认存在的日期与序列号，而"铆钉"像一根带电的线一样穿过了那段历史。他一直在从这些残骸上拆零件，搭建最后一具试验框架，并在场区里布置"教训"，好让任何靠近的人被压垮，同时整合那些证明"究竟是谁偷了工"的遥测与设计日志。若他在这里完工，证据会在一股扭曲金属与泄压空气的烟柱中消失，而他从未自一名游骑兵的战地笔记追到这片墓地的"安静灾难"模式，就会变成太空劫匪假装不记得的又一则传闻：尘土中数据板上的匿名图纸、火卫二上被抹除的审计，以及一条由同一只无形之手拯救或击碎的船只的线索。

#en: The PX-3446 hangs dead in the dark, a UC SysDef hull that should have been quietly towed and buried but instead left drifting just outside the busy lanes, where only someone following the wrong kind of math would think to look. Inside, the blast-sheared corridors and frozen fire doors say "training accident" to any official report, yet every sealed compartment hums with the sense of work interrupted just before it named a culprit. This is where field data and private suspicions were burned into the ship's memory banks, far from the committee rooms where admirals now swear they saw only random failures. The wreck is less a tomb than a locked filing cabinet, holding the one record of how Diego's patterns bled into military jumps, and why those who noticed chose to keep that knowledge in vacuum, not daylight. Up to now the trail has been whispers and half-truths: a dying captain's complaints on a forgotten rock, nervous route-sellers speaking off the record in a station bar, and scattered flight plans marked "mishap" that all shared the same quiet signature curling back to the same hand on the console.
zh: PX-3446死寂地悬在黑暗中，一具本该被悄悄拖走埋葬、却被留在繁忙航道外侧漂着联殖星防队船壳——只有追寻"错误类型数学"的人才会想到去看那里。在它内部，被爆炸剪开的走廊与冻结的防火门对任何官方报告来说都是"训练事故"，可每一个密封舱室都嗡鸣着"工作在被指认罪魁之前恰好中断"的感觉。这里正是实地数据与私人怀疑被烧进舰船记忆库的地方，远离那些海军上将如今发誓"只看到随机故障"的委员会会议室。这具残骸与其说是坟墓，不如说是一个锁着的档案柜，藏着"迭戈的模式如何渗进军事跃迁"的唯一记录，以及那些注意到的人为何选择把这份知识留在真空、而非日光下。到目前为止，这条线索是低语与半真半假：一块被遗忘岩石上一名垂死船长的抱怨、某家星际站酒吧里小声说话的紧张航路贩子，以及零散标着"事故"的飞行计划——它们都共享同一道安静签名，蜷曲回同一只搭在控制台上的手。

#en: Out here, the rock itself hums with the residue of what he has been doing. The mining complex was never built to host Grav Drive arrays, yet the shafts run straight into dense veins that bend readings, masking field tests from distant UC sensors and Freestar patrols alike. In these tunnels he can hide unstable prototypes between loaders and ore hoppers, burn stolen fuel, and dump irradiated slag into the walls while the workers call it a bad day in the drills. This is where his pattern converges where every anomalous route, every missing crate, every grav spike along the hauler lanes finally points. By the time the alarms trip, he will be one trigger pull from erasing the last proof of his part in the tender misjump and stepping fully into the shadows he helped Rhys open. The earliest version of how this began has already been traded away in bar stories and half wiped logs, but the trail is clear enough now remote datapads with scrambled signatures, a silent recorder drifting in orbit, hushed talk in a farming settlement, and a bruised asteroid field full of broken echoes all narrowing toward this buried heart.
zh: 在这里，岩石本身都因他一直在做的事而嗡鸣。那座采矿综合体从不是为承载引力引擎阵列而建，可那些竖井直通能扭曲读数的致密矿脉，把实地测试同时向远方联殖传感器与自由星系联盟巡逻掩藏。在这些隧道里，他能在装载机与矿石漏斗之间藏起不稳定的原型、烧掉偷来的燃料，并把受辐照的矿渣倒进岩壁，而工人们只当那是钻探倒霉的一天。这里正是他的模式汇聚之处——货船航线上每一道异常航线、每一个失踪货箱、每一个引力尖峰，最终都指向这里。等到警报触发时，他离"抹掉自己在温柔错跳中所扮演角色的最后证据、并彻底走进他帮里斯打开的那些阴影"只差一次扳机。这一切如何开始的最早版本早已在酒吧故事与半擦除日志里被交易掉了，但如今这条线索足够清晰：远程数据板上被搅乱的签名、轨道上一台漂着的沉默记录仪、一座农业定居点里的低声谈话，以及一片满是破碎回声的瘀伤小行星带，全都收窄向这颗被埋藏的心脏。

#en: The skymaps all say this mining pit should be quiet rock and thin air, yet the clouds above it twist like something half-tamed and half-feral, caught between vacuum and storm. Stormglass chose this scar in the crust for a reason: the drills already pierce deep seams, the Helium-3 lines and old grav infrastructure hum beneath the surface, and the thin atmosphere responds faster than any regulated world. Here she can fold every lesson and every mistake into one last experiment, trying to rewrite the hyperstorm that ruined her life by bleeding reactor exhaust and microclimate tweaks into the open sky. A single miscalculated correction from her early models turned one settlement into a grave; left alone, what she is forcing through the rock and air here could echo across systems.  \nWe traced her from a stray dataslate in the back end of nowhere to Ranger logs and worried technicians at a supply post, then through a strained Helium-3 facility running odd atmospheric diagnostics and a raider command site choked in storm-scoured rubble; every step pointed to the same pattern of tampered skies and abandoned safeguards.
zh: 所有的星图都说这个矿坑该是安静的岩石与稀薄空气，可它上方的云却像某种半驯服、半野性的东西般扭曲，卡在真空与风暴之间。"风暴玻璃"选中地壳上这道伤疤是有原因的：钻头本就穿透深层矿脉，氦-3 管线与旧引力基础设施在地表之下嗡鸣，而稀薄大气比任何受监管世界响应得更快。在这里，她能把每一课与每一个错误折进最后一次实验，试图通过把反应堆废气与微气候微调渗进露天天空，来改写那场毁掉她人生的超级风暴。她早期模型里一次算错的修正就把一座定居点变成了坟墓；任其自行，她此刻正从岩层与空气里强推出去的东西，可能在多个星系间回响。  \n我们从天涯之外一块散落数据板追到她，到游骑兵日志与某座补给站忧心的技师，然后穿过一座做着古怪大气诊断的紧张氦-3 设施与一处被风暴刮蚀的碎石塞满的掠夺者指挥场址；每一步都指向同样的模式：被动手脚的天空与被弃置的保障措施。

#en: The Well is where forgotten things are supposed to sink and stay down, drowned beneath tourist gloss and MAST rhetoric. Down here, records get lost, debts get rolled into shadows, and faces blur into the press of the crowd. For a man who lives by erasing people on paper, this undercity is the perfect last staging ground, close enough to GalBank's veins to tap them, low enough that no one in the towers wants to look too hard. He has been threading everything toward this point, consolidating false identities, liquidating hijacked claims, and preparing to cut loose from the Settled Systems with a ledger wiped clean. The quietly reassigned freighters in the drift, the altered case files beneath the plazas, the corrupted manifests hidden in Trade Authority holds were all pieces of the same exit strategy. Someone in the core tried to smother what they found, but the story kept leaking through bar talk and ruined captains. From that first stray dataslate in the black, to the nervous clerk in the city above, to the corrupted support ship parked off the main lanes, every whisper has led back to this pressure sink under New Atlantis.
zh: 深井区，是遗忘之物本应沉下去、留在下面的地方，淹在旅游亮面与三头同盟话术之下。在这下面，记录会丢失、债务会滚进阴影、面孔会在人群的涌动中模糊。对一个靠"在纸面上抹掉人"为生的人来说，这座下城是完美的最后一个集结点：离盖尔银行的血脉足够近、能把管子伸进去，又足够低、让高楼里没人愿意细看。他一直在把一切穿向这一点：整合假身份、变现被劫持的索赔，并准备带着一本擦干净的账册切断与定居星系的联系。漂流带里被悄悄改派的货船、广场下方被改动的案卷、藏在贸易管理局货舱里的损坏舱单，都是同一套撤离策略的碎片。核心区有人试图把他们的发现闷死，可这故事不断从酒吧闲谈与完蛋船长的口中漏出来。从漆黑中第一块散落数据板，到楼上城市里那名紧张的文书，再到停在主航道外的损坏支援船，每一句低语都被引回新亚特兰蒂斯城下方这个压力沉淀区。

#en: The Abandoned Bionics Lab sits at the end of every line you have pulled, a dead facility with live power and just enough automated systems left for someone like her to bend into a private theater. Here the tools are already in the walls: surgical bays, dormant prosthetic rigs, and half-coded interface suites she can wake with a keystroke, all buried far from regulators and still wired to old Ryujin standards she helped design. Out here she can finish stitching together the network hinted at in stolen firmware archives and smuggling ledgers, using the last intact equipment to tune a free mesh that would slip past any corporate leash, then ghost away behind her augmented clients. The scorched access door and a half-completed breach charge suggest another crew tried to end this and never made it past the first line of defenses. So far the trail reads like this: a forgotten dataslate in the back of beyond, ghost references to missing neuroamp designs in a quiet research outpost, then this same lab half-lit and full of erased logs, pointing to Splice circling back to weaponize the only place that still remembers how to build her.
zh: 那座废弃仿生学实验室位于你拉出的每一条线的尽头，一座带着电力的死设施，剩下的自动化系统刚好够像她那样的人把它掰成私人剧场。这里的工具已在墙里：手术舱、休眠的义体设备，以及她一个按键就能唤醒的半编码接口套件，全都埋在远离监管者之处，仍接在她参与设计的旧龙神标准上。在这外面，她能完成把被盗固件档案与走私账册里暗示的网络缝在一起，用最后完好的设备调校一张能溜过任何公司牵引的自由网格，然后藏到她的增强客户背后消失。被烧焦的入口门与一枚半完成的破门炸药说明，另有一支队伍曾试图终结这一切，却从没闯过第一道防线。目前为止，这条线索读起来是这样：天涯之外一块被遗忘的数据板、某座安静研究前哨里对失踪神经增幅器设计的幽灵引用，然后就是这同一座半亮、塞满被擦除日志的实验室，指向"拼接"绕回、要把唯一仍记得如何建造她的地方武器化。

#en: This part of Akila is where ships come to die slow, and the people who worked them are not far behind, which is exactly why any talk worth hearing sinks into the rust instead of floating up to the Core. Between leaning shacks and crooked repair stalls, actuators and grav rings pile in heaps, tagged with half-legible IDs from haulers that vanished on routes no insurance adjuster wants to audit too closely. The junction buried under all this clutter is not just scrap; it is a scar from a job that went wrong in a very specific way, a place where someone tested how far they could bend a flight path before it snapped. To pick through it here, at the edge of polite notice, is to step into a conversation every spacer in this quarter pretends they are not having, their words clipped short and eyes sliding away whenever timing, discounts, or a certain unseen navigator come up. So far, all you have are a half-burned dataslate from a forgotten camp and low-voiced rumors from worn-out haulers, enough to suggest that some jumps are being nudged off true and that the same quiet signature keeps surfacing wherever wreckage and bad luck pile together.
zh: 阿基拉城的这个区，是船只前来慢慢死去的地方，而开它们的人也紧跟其后，这正是为什么任何值得一听的谈话都会沉进锈里、而不会浮上核心区。在倾斜陋屋与歪斜修理摊之间，执行器与引力环堆成一堆，贴着半可辨认的 ID——它们来自那些在无人愿意细审的航线上消失的货船。埋在这堆杂物下的那个枢纽不只是废料；它是一桩以非常特定方式出错的工作留下的伤疤，一处有人测试"能在飞行路径断裂前把它掰弯多远"的地方。在这里、在体面注意的边缘翻检它，就是踏进一场这个区每个太空劫匪都假装自己没在进行的对话——他们的字句被削短，每当时机、折扣或某位看不见的领航员被提起，目光就滑开。目前为止，你只有一块来自被遗忘营地的半烧毁数据板与疲惫货船船员的低声传闻，足以暗示某些跃迁正被推离真实，而同样的安静签名不断在残骸与霉运堆积之处浮现。

#en: This outpost was never meant to matter; just another research shell on a quiet rock, built for routine data pulls and then half forgotten as priorities drifted elsewhere. That is what makes it perfect for what she did to it. When departments shifted, staff rotated, and oversight thinned to the occasional automated ping, the traffic through here kept flowing on old schedules, half monitored and half ignored. Somewhere in that slow slide from purpose to neglect, someone rewired a single exchange a handshake that once just synced survey results now brushes past LIST archives, Trade Authority ledgers, and settlement queues before vanishing into blank space. If I can pry open what is left of that link, I can see which chains she broke on purpose and which ones she quietly grafted together. Up to now all I have are scattered signs a dead end contact who asked the wrong question, a sealed lab with its logs scrubbed too clean, a nervous broker on Neon fencing partial routes, a derelict survey cutter with half a jump plan and every fragment points to her carefully bending systems over time, until nobody remembers what they were built to do in the first place.
zh: 这座前哨本不该有任何意义；不过是安静岩石上又一个研究外壳，为常规数据拉取而建，随后在优先级漂移时被半遗忘。这正是她把它变成现在这样的完美条件。当部门轮换、人员调动、监督稀薄成偶尔的自动脉冲时，经过这里的交通仍按旧日程流动，一半被监控、一半被忽视。在那场从"用途"滑向"忽视"的缓慢过程里，有人在某处重接了一次交换——一次曾只同步勘探结果握手，如今擦过独立盟档案、贸易管理局账册与定居点队列，然后消失在空白区域。若我能撬开那条连接剩下的东西，我就能看出她故意扯断了哪些链、又悄悄嫁接了哪些。到目前为止，我只有零散的迹象：一名问了错误问题的死掉联系人、一座日志被擦得太干净的密封实验室、霓虹城一名兜售部分航线的紧张掮客、一艘带着半份跃迁计划的弃置勘探切割船；每一块碎片都指向她小心地随时间弯折系统，直到没人记得它们最初被造来做什么。

#en: The Abandoned Deimos Scrapyard is where her whole crusade was always heading, a place built on the lie that wrecks are just metal and not the people written out of the manifests. Here, among gutted hulls and stripped grav drives, she is threading the last of her stolen data through hidden cores, preparing to erase or broadcast everything the salvage ring buried under "administrative resolutions." UC and Freestar patrols turned blind eyes to this yard for years, calling it obsolete while she turned it into a fortress and an archive in one. The rusted cranes, mined walkways, and jury-rigged turrets are not simply defenses but levers; if she finishes locking her ledgers here, the ghost-insured ships become more than rumor and the factions complicit in their loss may burn or double down. This is the last gap before the graveyards belong entirely to her or are swallowed again by the same silence that let her work go unnoticed for so long. So far, the trail has run from a discarded report in the dust to a sabotaged relay that throttled distress calls, then into a derelict UC combat ship whose untouched logs showed military routes overlapping "accidental" civilian disappearances.
zh: 那座"废弃火卫二废料场"，是她整场圣战一直朝着去的地方，一座建立在"残骸只是金属、而非被写出舱单的人"这个谎言之上的地方。在这里、在被掏空的船壳与被剥光的引力引擎之间，她把最后一批偷来的数据穿进隐藏核心，准备抹掉或广播那伙打捞集团埋在"行政决议"之下的一切。联殖与自由星系联盟巡逻队多年来对这片场区视而不见，在它变成堡垒兼档案馆时称它过时。那些锈蚀吊车、布雷步道与临时拼凑炮塔不只是防御，更是杠杆；若她完成把自己账册锁在这里，那些被"幽灵保险"的船就会不再只是传闻，而共谋其损失的派系或将焚毁、或将加注。这是最后一道缝隙——在那之后，墓地要么完全属于她，要么再次被那种"让她的工作长期不被注意"的同样沉默吞掉。目前为止，线索从尘土里一份被丢弃报告，到一座扼杀遇险呼叫的被动过手脚中继，然后钻进一艘弃置联殖战斗舰——它未被动过的日志显示军用航线与"意外"民用失踪重叠。
